title: The Hokkaido Birth Cohort Study on Environment and Children's Health: cohort profile-updated 2017.
ehr_evidence: Parent and infant medical records were obtained from physicians at the participating hospitals or clinics; data were collected via self-administered questionnaires, face-to-face neurobehavioral tests, and biospecimen measurements (maternal/cord blood, placenta, maternal hair, breast milk, household dust, child urine).
summary: A 2017 cohort profile of the prospective Hokkaido Birth Cohort Study (Sapporo cohort n=514 and Hokkaido cohort n=20,926) examining associations between low-level prenatal environmental chemical exposures (dioxins, PCBs, PFASs, phthalates, bisphenol A, methylmercury) and birth outcomes, growth, neurobehavioral development, allergies, and infectious diseases in Japanese children.
key_findings: PFOS negatively associated with birth weight (per log10 unit: β = −269.4 g, 95% CI −465.7 to −73.0)
PFOA negatively associated with ponderal index (per log10 unit: β = −0.73 kg/m3, 95% CI −1.44 to −0.02)
2,3,4,7,8-PeCDF had a significant negative influence on birth weight (per log10 unit: β = −24.5 g, 95% CI −387.4 to −61.5)
DEHP significantly decreased ponderal index (per log10 unit: β = −1.28, 95% CI −2.43 to −0.13)
PFOA negatively associated with mental development in 6-month-old girls (per log10 unit: β = −0.296, 95% CI −11.96 to −0.682)
Higher maternal PFTrDA levels decreased eczema risk at 24 months (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.45–0.86)
PFHxS associated with higher risk of total infectious disease among girls (OR 1.55, 95% CI 0.976–2.45)
IGF2 methylation inversely associated with PFOA levels; ~one fifth of PFOA effects on reduced ponderal index mediated by IGF2 methylation
Maternal smoking combined with AhR/CYP1A1 genetic variations reduced infant birth weight (e.g., −315 g)
Log10 Σdioxin associated with increased infant FT4 (β = 0.224 ng/dL, 95% CI 0.016 to 0.433)
2,3,4,7,8-pentachlorodibenzo-furan associated with increased risk of otitis media (OR 5.3, 95% CI 1.5–19)
captured_features: reproductive/steroid hormones (cortisol, DHEA, testosterone, estradiol, prolactin)
cord blood DNA methylation (IGF2, H19, LINE1)
pathologies_diseases: allergies (eczema, wheezing, food allergy, allergic rhino-conjunctivitis)
study_design: prospective birth cohort (nested case-cohort design applied to the large Hokkaido cohort)
data_source_type: birth cohort with biospecimen and questionnaire data
population: Pregnant women in Sapporo cohort (n=514, enrolled 23–35 weeks gestation) and Hokkaido cohort (n=20,926, enrolled <13 weeks gestation) in Hokkaido, Japan; offspring followed from birth through school age
exposure_domain: environmental chemicals / endocrine disruptors (dioxins, PCBs, PFASs, phthalates, bisphenol A, methylmercury)
limitations: loss to follow-up at birth and differential participation characteristics
relatively small Sapporo cohort limiting power for some analyses
relatively low exposure levels in the population limiting detection of associations
some exposure assessment relied on self-report
